text:
The chamber at Pellham Borough Council smells faintly of floor polish and old rain, and on the evening of 14 March 2024 it filled early. Harbour traders sat in the public gallery, coats still damp, watching a debate the town has circled for the better part of a generation.

Pellham's quays have long run on goodwill and patchwork funding. Dredging, sea-wall repairs and berth upkeep have each been paid for by emergency grants, never by any settled arrangement.

Councillor Odette Varnham, chair of the Pellham Harbour Committee, moved the levy motion. It sets a charge of 2.4% on commercial mooring and cargo-handling fees, projected to raise £1.8 million over five years.

The certified minutes of that regular evening session record the roll-call result: 19 to 6 in favour. The levy carried, and the harbour's long argument over who pays for it has, for now, been settled.
